newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil prices firm on household demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil prices firm on household demand.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices firmed nearly 500 rupees per tonne in the past week on increased household demand amid lower arrivals as farmers held back stocks, industry officials and traders said on Wednesday.
They expected prices to stabilise at this level.
"Demand is absolutely steady and has stopped further erosion in prices," Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange told Reuters.
Shah said demand for edible oil rose in December as most households buy their entire annual requirement during this period.
"Imports are also tapering off," Shah added.
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 35,000-36,000 rupees per tonne. Palm olein traded at around 28,300 rupees per tonne and soy oil was quoted at nearly 28,200 rupees per tonne.
"Crop arrivals were lower than last week. Farmers are holding back stocks at lower levels," Shah said.
Last week, industry officials said edible oil prices were expected to dip by 500 rupees per tonne after optimum arrivals in end-December.
Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said on Tuesday India's winter oilseed output in 1996/97 (November-October) was projected at 12.7 million tonnes against a target of 12.4 million.
He told the Indian parliament the current year's oilseed production was around 700,000 tonnes higher than last year's winter output of 12.01 million tonnes.
India harvests two oilseed crops annually, with the bulk of its output from the winter crop. The winter crop is sown in July and harvested from October onwards.
But trade estimates project this year's winter crop at 11.91 million tonnes, only marginally up from 11.43 million last year. --New Delhi newsroom +91-11-301 2024
